back: Mg: very slow (cold), fast with steam → MgO. Ca, Sr, Ba: M + 2H₂O → M(OH)₂ + H₂, more vigorous down the group.
MCO₃ → MO + CO₂; stability increases down the group.
2M(NO₃)₂ → 2MO + 4NO₂ + O₂ (brown fumes); stability increases down the group.
Hydroxides: more soluble down the group. Sulfates: less soluble down the group.
Mg brilliant white; Ca brick-red; Sr crimson; Ba apple-green.

front: Why Ca, Sr, Ba stop reacting with dilute H₂SO₄
back: An insoluble sulfate coats the metal (or carbonate) and keeps the acid away.
MgO furnace linings; CaO, Ca(OH)₂, CaCO₃ neutralise acid soils; CaCO₃ for cement, glass and iron extraction.
CaSO₄ plaster; BaSO₄ barium meal (insoluble, X-ray opaque); Mg(OH)₂ and magnesium trisilicate antacids.
Increases down the group: larger atoms, lower ionisation energies, outer electrons lost more easily.
